case.believed: Session.close makes every ORM attribute inaccessible, expire_on_commit=False keeps lazy relationships available after close, and loading a relationship before a default commit keeps it available on the detached object.
contract: The default expire_on_commit=True expires both previously loaded scalar attributes and relationships on commit; closing immediately afterward makes either access raise DetachedInstanceError.
Session.close without commit detaches the object but preserves already loaded scalar values, while an unloaded lazy relationship still raises DetachedInstanceError.
expire_on_commit=False preserves scalar values through commit and close but does not load a lazy relationship, so detached relationship access still fails.
selectinload loads a relationship before detachment, allowing both the scalar and relationship collection to be read after Session.close when no commit expires them.
Session.refresh with attribute_names can explicitly load a relationship before close so the detached collection remains readable.
case.goal: Prove SQLAlchemy 2.0.44 expire_on_commit and Session.close detached-instance boundaries for scalar and relationship access, including selectinload and refresh remedies.
